Evidence lists several Phase 3 (including Phase 2/3) lung cancer trials involving pembrolizumab (Keytruda). Trials where pembrolizumab is the main tested drug or a comparator:
- NCT02142738: Pembrolizumab vs platinum-based chemotherapies in metastatic NSCLC (KEYNOTE-024), Phase 3, Completed [trial:NCT02142738].
- NCT03302234: Pembrolizumab with ipilimumab or placebo in untreated metastatic NSCLC (KEYNOTE-598), Phase 3, Completed [trial:NCT03302234].
- NCT01905657: Two doses of pembrolizumab vs docetaxel in previously treated NSCLC (KEYNOTE-010), Phase 2/3, Completed [trial:NCT01905657].
- NCT05226598: Pembrolizumab/vibostolimab coformulation plus chemotherapy vs pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in metastatic NSCLC (KEYVIBE-007), Phase 3, Terminated [trial:NCT05226598].
- NCT05722015: Subcutaneous pembrolizumab with berahyaluronidase alfa vs IV pembrolizumab in metastatic NSCLC (MK-3475A-D77), Phase 3, Active not recruiting [trial:NCT05722015].
Trials where pembrolizumab is a comparator or backbone for another drug:
- NCT06561386: Nivolumab and relatlimab plus chemotherapy vs pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in stage IV/recurrent non-squamous NSCLC, Phase 3, Recruiting [trial:NCT06561386].
- NCT07063745: Navlimetostat (BMS-986504) with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy vs placebo plus pembrolizumab and chemotherapy in MTAP-deleted metastatic NSCLC, Phase 2/3, Recruiting [trial:NCT07063745].
- NCT05502237: Zimberelimab and domvanalimab plus chemotherapy vs pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in untreated metastatic NSCLC, Phase 3, Active not recruiting [trial:NCT05502237].
- NCT05791097: Ociperlimab with tislelizumab and chemotherapy in locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, Phase 3, Withdrawn; pembrolizumab is listed as an intervention [trial:NCT05791097].
NCT04322617 (anlotinib plus immune checkpoint inhibitors, Phase 2/3) does not name pembrolizumab in the evidence [trial:NCT04322617].

Two recruiting trials of semaglutide list heart failure and include a Phase 3 component, and a third recruiting trial does not list semaglutide. 1) NCT06082063, Multifactorial Intervention to Reduce Cardiovascular Disease in Type 1 Diabetes: Phase 3, Recruiting; interventions include semaglutide, and heart failure is a listed condition [trial:NCT06082063]. 2) NCT06423599, Effect of Weight Loss on Physical and Cardiac Performance in People With Obesity and Heart Failure: Phase 2/Phase 3, Recruiting; it tests semaglutide injectable product versus a calorie-restricted diet [trial:NCT06423599]. NCT07223242 (Tailored Exercise Training Study Among Adults With HFpEF) is Phase 2/3 and recruiting, but its listed interventions are exercise training and weight loss, not semaglutide [trial:NCT07223242]. Only NCT06082063 is a pure Phase 3 trial.

Yes. The evidence lists recruiting dupilumab trials for eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE):
- NCT06695897: Non-interventional observational study of long-term efficacy and safety of dupilumab in patients >=12 years with EoE in Germany; phase n/a; RECRUITING [trial:NCT06695897].
- NCT07112378: A Study of Dupilumab in Small Children With an Allergic Condition of the Esophagus (EoE); Phase 3; RECRUITING [trial:NCT07112378].
- NCT06705387: Dupilumab Versus Topical Corticosteroid Effectiveness - Comparison in the Treatment of Stenotic EoE; Phase 2; RECRUITING [trial:NCT06705387].
- NCT06665971: Effect of Dupilumab on the Muscle Function of the Esophagus in Participants with EoE; Phase 4; RECRUITING [trial:NCT06665971].
Related but not strictly EoE-specific: NCT07257835, Dupilumab Therapy for EGIDs (eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorders); phase n/a; RECRUITING [trial:NCT07257835].
NCT07012928 is a recruiting EoE study, but no dupilumab intervention is listed for it [trial:NCT07012928].

Phase 2 (including Phase 1/2) trials involving olaparib in prostate cancer found in the evidence:
- NCT03570476, Olaparib Before Surgery in Treating Participants With Localized Prostate Cancer, Phase 2, Terminated [trial:NCT03570476].
- NCT03516812, Testosterone and Olaparib in Treating Patients With Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer, Phase 2, Completed [trial:NCT03516812].
- NCT05262608, The Study of Olaparib in Newly Diagnosed mCRPC Patients With HRR Gene Mutation, Phase 2, Unknown [trial:NCT05262608].
- NCT05005728, XmAb20717 (Vudalimab) Alone or in Combination With Chemotherapy or Targeted Therapy in Patients With mCRPC (includes a vudalimab + olaparib arm), Phase 2, Completed [trial:NCT05005728].
- NCT05568550, Pembro With Radiation With or Without Olaparib, Phase 2, Recruiting [trial:NCT05568550].
- NCT04748042, Focal Radiation With Pulsed Systemic Therapy of Abiraterone, ADT, Lynparza Towards Castration Sensitive Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer (FAALCON), Phase 2, Active not recruiting [trial:NCT04748042].
- NCT03810105, A Study of Olaparib and Durvalumab in Prostate Cancer, Phase 2, Terminated [trial:NCT03810105].
- NCT04556617, PLX2853 in Combination With Abiraterone Acetate and Prednisone and in Combination With Olaparib in mCRPC, Phase 1/2, Terminated [trial:NCT04556617].
- NCT06065059, Study to Evaluate TNG348 Alone and With a PARP Inhibitor in Patients With BRCA 1/2 Mutant or HRD+ Solid Tumors (prostate cancer among the conditions), Phase 1/2, Terminated [trial:NCT06065059].

NCT06401980 (darolutamide in mCRPC) lists no olaparib intervention, so it is excluded [trial:NCT06401980].

Two trials in the evidence test tirzepatide for obstructive sleep apnea. NCT07846865: Tirzepatide Versus Positive Airway Pressure for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnoea: A Randomised Comparative Effectiveness Trial; Phase 2/3; Not yet recruiting [trial:NCT07846865]. NCT05412004: Obstructive Sleep Apnea Master Protocol GPIF: A Study of Tirzepatide (LY3298176) in Participants With Obstructive Sleep Apnea; Phase 3; Completed [trial:NCT05412004]. A third trial, NCT06400615 (AD109 in patients taking GLP-1 drugs), does not list tirzepatide as an intervention, so it is not a tirzepatide trial [trial:NCT06400615].

Completed trials in atrial fibrillation that list apixaban as an intervention and are Phase 3 (or Phase 2/3):
- NCT02933697: Compare Apixaban and Vitamin-K Antagonists in Patients With AF and ESKD; Phase 3; Completed [trial:NCT02933697].
- NCT00496769: A Phase III Study of Apixaban in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation; Phase 3; Completed [trial:NCT00496769].
- NCT00412984: Apixaban for the Prevention of Stroke in Subjects With Atrial Fibrillation; Phase 3; Completed [trial:NCT00412984].
- NCT02283294: Apixaban for Early Prevention of Recurrent Embolic Stroke and Hemorrhagic Transformation; Phase 3; Completed [trial:NCT02283294].
- NCT02889562: Apixaban Versus Warfarin for the Management of Post-operative Atrial Fibrillation; Phase 2/3; Completed [trial:NCT02889562].
- NCT03153150: Start or STop Anticoagulants Randomised Trial (SoSTART); Phase 3; Completed [trial:NCT03153150].
- NCT03996772: PREvention of STroke in Intracerebral haemorrhaGE Survivors With Atrial Fibrillation; Phase 3; Completed [trial:NCT03996772].
- NCT03181386: Tooth Extraction in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation in Use of New Oral Anticoagulants; Phase 3; Completed [trial:NCT03181386].
NCT01924065 (post-cardioversion stroke risk) is also Phase 3 and Completed, but it lists only cardioversion and an unspecified oral anticoagulant, not apixaban specifically [trial:NCT01924065].

Recruiting trials involving nivolumab (or Opdivo) in hepatocellular carcinoma:
- NCT07176650, HLX13 (ipilimumab biosimilar) vs Yervoy as first-line for unresectable HCC (Interventions include OPDIVO), Phase 1, Recruiting [trial:NCT07176650].
- NCT05257590, CVM-1118 in Combination With Nivolumab for Unresectable Advanced HCC, Phase 2, Recruiting [trial:NCT05257590].
- NCT07482059, Multicenter Clinical Study of Combined Therapy for Unresectable HCC (yttrium-90 microspheres with nivolumab, ipilimumab, lenvatinib), Phase 1/2, Recruiting [trial:NCT07482059].
- NCT07075120, Ipilimumab and Nivolumab With SBRT in Locally Advanced Hepatocellular Cancer, Phase 1, Recruiting [trial:NCT07075120].
- NCT07689175, Adaptive Dosing of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors for HCC (nivolumab, ipilimumab), Phase 2, Recruiting [trial:NCT07689175].
- NCT04380545, Nivolumab, Fluorouracil, and Interferon Alpha 2B for Unresectable Fibrolamellar Cancer (conditions listed include stage III/IV HCC), Phase 1/2, Recruiting [trial:NCT04380545].
- NCT07147101, Different First-line Immunotherapy for Advanced HCC (observational; interventions include nivolumab and ipilimumab), Phase n/a, Recruiting [trial:NCT07147101].
- NCT07430202, DNAJB1-PRKACA peptide vaccine with DRP-104, nivolumab, and ipilimumab in advanced fibrolamellar carcinoma (fibrolamellar hepatocellular cancer), Phase 1, Recruiting [trial:NCT07430202].

NCT07100405 (PD-1 inhibitor with TACE) and NCT06422403 (extended dosing intervals) do not name nivolumab in their listed interventions, so they are not included.

NCT02339571 is a Phase II/III trial titled "A Phase II/III Trial of Nivolumab, Ipilimumab, and GM-CSF in Patients With Advanced Melanoma" [trial:NCT02339571]. It is sponsored by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) [trial:NCT02339571]. It is a randomized study comparing nivolumab plus ipilimumab plus sargramostim versus nivolumab plus ipilimumab in patients with unresectable Stage III or Stage IV melanoma [trial:NCT02339571]. It studies side effects and how well the treatments work, and aims to determine whether nivolumab and ipilimumab are more effective with or without sargramostim [trial:NCT02339571]. The primary outcome is overall survival [trial:NCT02339571]. Status is active, not recruiting, with enrollment of 600 and a start date of 2015-11-23 [trial:NCT02339571].
There are 207 Phase 2 ClinicalTrials.gov studies matching nivolumab in melanoma [count:1].
There are 169 ClinicalTrials.gov studies of semaglutide with a status of recruiting [count:1].
58 Phase 3 trials on ClinicalTrials.gov have studied adalimumab in rheumatoid arthritis [count:1].
There are 114 ClinicalTrials.gov studies registered for empagliflozin and heart failure [count:1].

The boxed warning for warfarin is "WARNING: BLEEDING RISK." Warfarin sodium can cause major or fatal bleeding [label:warfarin:boxed_warning:0]. Regular INR monitoring should be performed in all treated patients [label:warfarin:boxed_warning:0]. Drugs, dietary changes, and other factors affect INR levels achieved with warfarin therapy [label:warfarin:boxed_warning:0]. Patients should be instructed about prevention measures to minimize bleeding risk and to report signs and symptoms of bleeding [label:warfarin:boxed_warning:0].

Apixaban (ELIQUIS) is contraindicated in patients with active pathological bleeding [label:apixaban:contraindications:0]. It is also contraindicated in patients with severe hypersensitivity reaction to ELIQUIS, such as anaphylactic reactions [label:apixaban:contraindications:0].

Pembrolizumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds to the PD-1 receptor and blocks its interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, releasing PD-1 pathway-mediated inhibition of the immune response, including the anti-tumor immune response [label:pembrolizumab:mechanism_of_action:0]. Binding of PD-L1 and PD-L2 to PD-1 on T cells normally inhibits T cell proliferation and cytokine production [label:pembrolizumab:mechanism_of_action:0]. Some tumors upregulate PD-1 ligands, and signaling through this pathway can contribute to inhibition of active T-cell immune surveillance of tumors [label:pembrolizumab:mechanism_of_action:0]. In syngeneic mouse tumor models, blocking PD-1 activity decreased tumor growth [label:pembrolizumab:mechanism_of_action:0].

The isotretinoin label says it is contraindicated in pregnancy because it can cause fetal harm [label:isotretinoin:pregnancy:0]. The boxed warning states it can cause life-threatening birth defects, and there is an extremely high risk of them if pregnancy occurs while taking any amount, even for short periods [label:isotretinoin:boxed_warning:0]. Potentially any exposed fetus can be affected, and there is no accurate way to determine prenatally whether an exposed fetus has been affected [label:isotretinoin:boxed_warning:0].

Details:
- Human exposure is associated with an increased risk of major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, and premature births [label:isotretinoin:pregnancy:0]. Documented malformations involve the face, eyes, ears, skull, CNS, cardiovascular system, and thymus and parathyroid glands [label:isotretinoin:pregnancy:0].
- If pregnancy occurs during treatment, discontinue immediately and refer the patient to an obstetrician-gynecologist experienced in reproductive toxicity for evaluation and counseling [label:isotretinoin:boxed_warning:0].
- Suspected fetal exposure during or 1 month after treatment should be reported immediately to the FDA MedWatch and to the iPLEDGE pregnancy registry [label:isotretinoin:warnings_and_cautions:1].
- Because of the embryo-fetal toxicity risk, the drug is available only through the iPLEDGE REMS restricted program [label:isotretinoin:boxed_warning:0].
- In patients who can get pregnant, pregnancy testing is required before, during, and after treatment [label:isotretinoin:use_in_specific_populations:2].

The clopidogrel boxed warning is about diminished antiplatelet effect in patients with two loss-of-function alleles of the CYP2C19 gene [label:clopidogrel:boxed_warning:0]. Clopidogrel's effectiveness depends on conversion to an active metabolite by the CYP system, principally CYP2C19 [label:clopidogrel:boxed_warning:0]. At recommended doses, patients who are homozygous for nonfunctional CYP2C19 alleles (CYP2C19 poor metabolizers) form less of the active metabolite, so the effect on platelet activity is reduced [label:clopidogrel:boxed_warning:0]. Tests are available to identify CYP2C19 poor metabolizers [label:clopidogrel:boxed_warning:0]. The warning says to consider another platelet P2Y12 inhibitor in patients identified as poor metabolizers [label:clopidogrel:boxed_warning:0].

The ciprofloxacin boxed warning describes disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions that have occurred together, including tendinitis and tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, and central nervous system effects [label:ciprofloxacin:boxed_warning:0]. It also states that fluoroquinolones, including ciprofloxacin, may exacerbate muscle weakness in patients with myasthenia gravis, and that ciprofloxacin should be avoided in patients with a known history of myasthenia gravis [label:ciprofloxacin:boxed_warning:0]. The label says to discontinue ciprofloxacin immediately and avoid fluoroquinolones in patients who experience any of these serious adverse reactions [label:ciprofloxacin:boxed_warning:0]. Because of these risks, ciprofloxacin should be reserved for patients with no alternative treatment options for acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, acute uncomplicated cystitis, and acute sinusitis [label:ciprofloxacin:boxed_warning:2].

Dupilumab (DUPIXENT), an interleukin-4 receptor alpha antagonist, is indicated for several conditions [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:0]. Atopic dermatitis: moderate-to-severe AD in patients aged 6 months and older not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies or when those therapies are not advisable [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:0]. Asthma: add-on maintenance treatment in patients aged 6 years and older with moderate-to-severe eosinophilic-phenotype or oral corticosteroid-dependent asthma, not for acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:0]. Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: add-on maintenance treatment in patients aged 12 years and older with inadequately controlled CRSwNP [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:2]. Eosinophilic esophagitis: patients aged 1 year and older weighing at least 15 kg [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:2]. Prurigo nodularis: adults [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:2]. COPD: add-on maintenance treatment in adults with inadequately controlled COPD and an eosinophilic phenotype, not for acute bronchospasm [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:2]. Chronic spontaneous urticaria: patients aged 2 years and older who remain symptomatic despite H1 antihistamine treatment, not for other forms of urticaria [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:2]. Bullous pemphigoid: adults [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:3]. Allergic fungal rhinosinusitis: patients aged 6 years and older with a history of sino-nasal surgery [label:dupilumab:indications_and_usage:3].

The amiodarone boxed warning is titled "Pulmonary, Hepatic and Cardiac Toxicity" [label:amiodarone:boxed_warning:0]. Pulmonary toxicity (hypersensitivity pneumonitis or interstitial/alveolar pneumonitis) has caused clinically manifest disease at rates as high as 17% in some series, and has been fatal about 10% of the time [label:amiodarone:boxed_warning:0]. Hepatotoxicity can occur and can be fatal [label:amiodarone:boxed_warning:0]. Amiodarone can also exacerbate arrhythmias (proarrhythmic toxicity), so it should be initiated in a clinical setting with continuous electrocardiograms and cardiac resuscitation available [label:amiodarone:boxed_warning:0]. The warning states that its use is accompanied by substantial toxicity, some of it life-threatening, and that it is reserved for patients with indicated life-threatening arrhythmias [label:amiodarone:boxed_warning:1].

Ozempic (semaglutide) is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or in patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2) [label:semaglutide:contraindications:0]. It is also contraindicated in patients with a serious hypersensitivity reaction to semaglutide or to any of the excipients in OZEMPIC [label:semaglutide:contraindications:0]. Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and angioedema, have been reported with OZEMPIC [label:semaglutide:contraindications:0].

Eliquis (apixaban) has a boxed warning with two parts. (A) Premature discontinuation increases the risk of thrombotic events: premature discontinuation of any oral anticoagulant, including ELIQUIS, increases this risk [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:0]. If anticoagulation is stopped for a reason other than pathological bleeding or completion of a course of therapy, consider coverage with another anticoagulant [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:0]. (B) Spinal/epidural hematoma: epidural or spinal hematomas may occur in patients receiving neuraxial anesthesia or undergoing spinal puncture, and these may result in long-term or permanent paralysis [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:0]. Factors that can increase this risk include indwelling epidural catheters, concomitant use of other drugs that affect hemostasis (such as NSAIDs, platelet inhibitors, other anticoagulants), a history of traumatic or repeated epidural or spinal punctures, and a history of spinal deformity or spinal surgery [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:1]. The optimal timing between ELIQUIS administration and neuraxial procedures is not known [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:1]. Patients should be monitored frequently for signs and symptoms of neurological impairment, and urgent treatment is necessary if neurological compromise is noted [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:1].

Yes. Zoloft (sertraline) carries a boxed warning for suicidal thoughts and behaviors [label:sertraline:boxed_warning:0]. Antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients in short-term studies [label:sertraline:boxed_warning:0]. The label says to closely monitor all antidepressant-treated patients for clinical worsening and for emergence of suicidal thoughts and behaviors [label:sertraline:boxed_warning:0].

Lipitor (atorvastatin) is a selective, competitive inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme that converts HMG-CoA to mevalonate, a precursor of sterols including cholesterol [label:atorvastatin:mechanism_of_action:0]. In animal models, it lowers plasma cholesterol and lipoprotein levels by inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase and cholesterol synthesis in the liver, and by increasing the number of hepatic LDL receptors on the cell surface to enhance LDL uptake and catabolism [label:atorvastatin:mechanism_of_action:0]. It also reduces LDL production and the number of LDL particles [label:atorvastatin:mechanism_of_action:0].

Yes. ClinicalTrials.gov lists 144 Phase 3 studies matching pembrolizumab and lung cancer [count:1]. Examples: NCT01905657, Pembrolizumab (MK-3475) two doses vs docetaxel in previously treated NSCLC (KEYNOTE-010), Phase 2/3, Completed [trial:NCT01905657]; NCT03302234, Pembrolizumab with ipilimumab or placebo in untreated metastatic NSCLC (KEYNOTE-598), Phase 3, Completed [trial:NCT03302234]; NCT06561386, Nivolumab and relatlimab plus chemotherapy vs pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in stage IV/recurrent non-squamous NSCLC, Phase 3, Recruiting [trial:NCT06561386]. Common adverse reactions (reported in ≥20% of patients) with KEYTRUDA as a single agent were fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, rash, diarrhea, pyrexia, cough, decreased appetite, pruritus, dyspnea, constipation, pain, abdominal pain, nausea, and hypothyroidism [label:pembrolizumab:adverse_reactions:0]. With chemotherapy or chemoradiotherapy, common reactions included fatigue/asthenia, nausea, constipation, diarrhea, decreased appetite, rash, vomiting, cough, dyspnea, pyrexia, alopecia, and peripheral neuropathy, among others [label:pembrolizumab:adverse_reactions:0]. The label also describes severe and fatal immune-mediated adverse reactions and infusion-related reactions [label:pembrolizumab:adverse_reactions:0].

Yes. The registry count shows 13 recruiting ClinicalTrials.gov studies of empagliflozin in chronic kidney disease [count:2]. Examples with empagliflozin as an intervention: NCT07074418, Effect of Empagliflozin in Patients With eGFR Between 10 and 20 ml/Min/1.73m2, Phase 4, recruiting [trial:NCT07074418]; NCT06013865, Empagliflozin Treatment in Kidney Transplant Recipients, Phase 4, recruiting [trial:NCT06013865]; NCT06430684, Feasibility Trial of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Pediatric CKD, Early Phase 1, recruiting [trial:NCT06430684]; NCT06642272, Pragmatic Trial Comparing Empagliflozin and Dapagliflozin, Phase 4, recruiting [trial:NCT06642272]. Other recruiting trials in the evidence involve dialysis or end-stage kidney disease, such as NCT05786443, Safety and Efficacy of Empagliflozin in Hemodialysis, Phase 2 [trial:NCT05786443]. Only 10 trials were listed in the evidence, so the full set of 13 is not shown. Contraindication: the label lists only hypersensitivity to empagliflozin or any excipients in JARDIANCE, with reactions such as angioedema having occurred [label:empagliflozin:contraindications:0].
